record.one_liner: Discord is a chat, voice and community platform organized into servers (guilds) and channels, with a developer platform for bots and apps.
record.auth_notes: Bot token sent as `Authorization: Bot <token>` (from app settings; a static credential). OAuth2 for user-delegated access: authorization code (with PKCE), implicit (not recommended), client credentials (bearer for bot owner), bot authorization flow, and webhook flow. Access tokens are sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Basic auth (client_id:client_secret) applies only to the OAuth2 token endpoints. Incoming webhooks are an additional URL-based mechanism.
record.access_notes: Anyone with a free Discord account can create an application and bot in the developer portal. I did not fetch the portal page itself, so this is inferred from the docs' bot-token and OAuth2 flows. Some scopes need partner approval: dm_channels.read, rpc*, voice, identify.premium and applications.builds.upload. relationships.read needs an access request. Verified-bot status is needed to grow past the guild cap, and the docs page doesn't state the cap number or the criteria.
record.blocker: Bot actions work only in guilds where the bot is installed, and the user must add it. User-token actions are limited by OAuth scopes. Some scopes (DM channel reads, RPC, voice) are partner-only. Rate limits apply, and the docs say apps that ignore them can have their credentials revoked. Bots must send a DiscordBot User-Agent. A "docs.discord.com/mcp" docs-search endpoint was reported by a third party, but I couldn't confirm it on a Discord page, so I classed MCP as community.
